title: Education for Sustainable Development Bridging Human Health and Environment
original_quote: strives towards a world in which all humans have access to sufficient food and water, a healthy and productive life, basic education, and a safer and just environment.
context_analysis: The framework embeds sustainable development directly into education. By linking a "healthy and productive life" with the necessity of a "safer and just environment," it provides a macro-level curricular mandate to view human health as dependent on planetary stability and equitable resource distribution.

title: Linking Sexual Health and Sustainable Environments
original_quote: 8. I can articulate my personal responsibilities related to my sexual health, well-being and behaviour. 9. I can discuss issues related to a healthy and sustainable environment.
context_analysis: By juxtaposing personal health responsibilities alongside discussions about a healthy and sustainable environment within the same broad learning objectives, the syllabus conceptually integrates personal wellbeing with the broader necessity of environmental sustainability, reflecting the Planetary Health approach.

title: Integrating Health and Environmental Sustainability
original_quote: Subject Focus: Health, Safety and Well being... 22 I can talk about my responsibility towards the environment. 23 I can share my idea of a positive and healthy environment. 24 I can define and discuss the idea and practice of sustainability.
context_analysis: Grouping environmental responsibility and sustainability explicitly under the "Health, Safety and Well being" subject focus operationalizes Planetary Health. It structurally teaches students that human health and safety are intrinsically tied to environmental conservation and sustainable practices.

title: Linking Diet, Organic Food, and Carbon Footprints
original_quote: Subject Focus: Sustainable Resource Management 1. I can suggest ways of respecting the environment and give examples how to separate waste at source. 2. I can discuss environmental issues such as food miles, carbon footprint and food waste. 3. I can explain the benefits of organic food and list ways to include it in the diet.
context_analysis: This objective intertwines human dietary choices with ecological metrics like carbon footprints and food miles. By examining the environmental and health benefits of organic foods concurrently, it operationalizes the Planetary Health paradigm within resource management.

title: Evaluating Shopping Practices for Health and Sustainability
original_quote: 7.2p Outline rules for wise shopping keeping in mind value for money, health, hygiene, efficiency and sustainability. E.g. using a shopping list, buying in bulk, shopping local... reading nutrition and sustainability labels
context_analysis: This learning objective directs students to view consumer choices through a dual lens of human health (nutrition/hygiene) and environmental health (sustainability). It embeds Planetary Health by showing that everyday consumer decisions have correlated impacts on both personal biology and ecological systems.

title: Health, Wellbeing, and Sustainability Principles
original_quote: LO1 Demonstrate an understanding of health, wellbeing, and the principles of sustainability.
context_analysis: This overarching learning outcome explicitly pairs human health and wellbeing with the principles of sustainability. By making this a core objective, the curriculum mandates that students study human physical health as a concept fundamentally linked to sustainable environmental practices.

title: Traceability, Food Safety, and Public Health
original_quote: 4.2at Define traceability in the food supply chain to assist in the assurance of food safety and quality. 4.3at Explain the need for traceability for consumer safety... 4.3au Discuss the value of reporting of HACCP infringements and food poisoning incidences for public health.
context_analysis: By examining food safety and traceability in the supply chain, the curriculum touches upon the animal-human-environment interface of food production. Understanding how pathogens move through the food system to impact public health operationalizes One Health principles regarding food safety.

title: National Dietary Guidelines and Seasonal/Local Food
original_quote: 5.1ay Choose dishes that meet the requirements according to the assignment given whilst adhering to National Dietary Guidelines with some use of fresh, seasonal and local food.
context_analysis: The curriculum bridges formal human nutritional standards (National Dietary Guidelines) with environmentally sustainable agricultural practices (seasonal and local food). This instructs students to prioritize food systems that benefit both personal health and regional ecology.

title: Global Goals for Health and Sustainability
original_quote: 11 I value the importance of sustainable Development and the Global goals 'No Poverty', 'Zero Hunger', 'Good health and well-being' and 'Quality Education'
context_analysis: Integrating the UN Sustainable Development Goals into the curriculum exposes young learners to the macro-level interconnectedness of human thriving (Zero Hunger, Good Health) and global sustainable development. It lays a foundational understanding of Planetary Health.
